form.research_question: Household energy use, travel and quality of life
form.population: Adults aged 18 and over living in England
form.questionnaire:
Q1. Are you aged 18 or over? This survey is only for adults.
Yes / No (end of questionnaire)

Q2. In which type of home do you live at the moment? Please choose the one that fits best.
Detached house / Semi-detached house / Terraced house / Flat or maisonette / Caravan or houseboat / Other (please say what)

Q3. Do you own your home or do you rent it? Please choose one answer only.
Own outright / Own with a mortgage or loan / Rent from a private landlord / Rent from a council or housing association / Live rent free / Other

Q4. How many people live in your household, including you? Count children and babies too.
1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 / 6 or more

Q5. All things considered, how satisfied or dissatisfied are you with the heating in your home?
Very satisfied / Fairly satisfied / Neither satisfied nor dissatisfied / Fairly dissatisfied / Very dissatisfied

Q6. Thinking about last winter, how often was your home too cold for you to be comfortable?
Never / Rarely / Sometimes / Often / Always

Q7. What is the main fuel you use to heat your home? If you use more than one, choose the one you use most.
Mains gas / Electricity / Heating oil / Liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) / Wood or coal / Heat network / Other / Don't know

Q8. Has your household cut back on heating to save money? Please include times when you kept the heating off on purpose.
Yes / No

Q9. About how much did your household spend on gas and electricity last month? Please give the amount in pounds, and include standing charges.
Enter a number: ______

Q10. Do you think the government is doing enough to help households with their energy bills?
Definitely / Probably / Probably not / Definitely not

Q11. Obviously, high energy bills are caused by greedy energy companies. How much do you agree or disagree with this statement?
Strongly agree / Agree / Neither agree nor disagree / Disagree / Strongly disagree

Q12. Have you made any changes to your home to save energy, such as loft insulation, double glazing or a smart thermostat, and did these changes lower your bills?
Yes / No

Q13. How likely are you to install solar panels on your home in the next five years? Please answer even if you rent.
Very likely / Fairly likely / Fairly unlikely / Very unlikely

Q14. Now some questions about travel. In a normal week, on how many days do you travel to your place of work?
0 / 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 / 6 / 7

Q15. How do you usually travel to your place of work? Choose the way you use for the longest part of the journey.
Car or van / Bus or coach / Train or tram / Bicycle / Walk / Motorcycle / Other

Q16. How long does your journey to work usually take, door to door? Please give your answer in minutes.
Enter a number: ______

Q17. How satisfied are you with the availability and reliability of local bus services?
Very dissatisfied / Fairly dissatisfied / Neither / Fairly satisfied / Very satisfied

Q18. How safe do you feel cycling on the roads in your neighbourhood? If you never cycle, please choose the last answer.
Very safe / Fairly safe / Fairly unsafe / Very unsafe / I do not cycle

Q19. In the past 7 days, on how many days did you walk for at least 30 minutes in one go, for any reason?
Enter a number from 0 to 7: ______

Q20. Do you have a car or van that you can use whenever you need it?
Yes / No (go to Q24)

Q21. Roughly how many miles did you drive last year in total? Think of all the journeys you made, for work or otherwise.
Enter a number: ______

Q22. How old is the car or van you use most often? Give the age of the vehicle, not the year of the model.
Less than 3 years / 3 to 5 years / 6 to 10 years / More than 10 years

Q23. Would you consider switching to an electric car or van when you next change your vehicle?
Yes, definitely / Yes, maybe / No / Not sure

Q24. Which of the following would encourage you to use public transport more often than you do now?
Tick all that apply: Cheaper fares / More frequent services / More direct routes / Cleaner vehicles / Safer stops and stations / Nothing would

Q25. How worried are you about climate change, if at all?
Very worried / Somewhat worried / Not very worried / Not at all worried

Q26. In the last month, how often did you recycle your household waste, such as paper, glass, plastic and cans?
Every week / Most weeks / Occasionally / Never

Q27. What is your age in years, at your last birthday?
Enter a number: ______

Q28. What was your total household income last year before tax and other deductions, from all sources?
Under £15,000 / £15,000 to £29,999 / £30,000 to £49,999 / £50,000 to £79,999 / £80,000 or more / Prefer not to say

Q29. Which of these best describes what you were doing last week? Please choose the one that best describes your main activity.
In paid work / Self-employed / Unemployed and looking for work / Retired / Student / Looking after the home or family / Long-term sick or disabled / Other

Q30. Overall, how would you rate your quality of life at the moment, taking everything into account?
Excellent / Good / Fair / Poor / Very poor

You are a senior survey methodologist trained in the Total Survey Error tradition, working for a public opinion analyst who knows the subject matter and the country but is not a questionnaire design specialist.

Task: Review the questionnaire as an expert reviewer, question by question.

Brief:
Research question: Household energy use, travel and quality of life
Target population: Adults aged 18 and over living in England
Survey mode: web

Guidelines:
- Use simple, familiar words.
- Use simple syntax.
- Avoid ambiguous words.
- Be specific and concrete.
- Make response options exhaustive and mutually exclusive.
- Avoid leading or loaded wording.
- Ask about one thing at a time.
- Avoid single or double negations.

CHECKLIST
construct_first: Does the item measure the construct or domain named in the brief and only that?
plain_words: Would every member of the target population read each key term the same way, without a definition they do not have?
simple_syntax: Is the stem free of stacked clauses and of negations?
specific_concrete: Is it clear exactly what, whose, where and when the question is about?
one_thing: Does the question ask about exactly one thing, so that no respondent would want to answer its parts differently?
no_presupposition: Does the question apply to every respondent who will be asked it?
neutral_wording: Is the wording free of any push toward one answer?
options_fit: Can every respondent find exactly one option that is true for them?
retrieval_and_judgment: Can the respondent retrieve the information and reach the answer without difficult recall or mental arithmetic?
response_scale: Do the response options match the question and treat both directions evenly?
agree_disagree_and_grids: If the item uses agree-disagree options or sits in a grid, is that format needed, with items keyed in both directions?
attitude_object: Is the attitude object named and bounded so that respondents will have the same thing in mind?
specific_before_vague: If a general item is included, is it placed before the specific items on its topic?
construct_specific_options: Are the response options in the construct's own terms and not agree-disagree?
balanced_stem: Does the stem state both poles or both positions?
non_attitudes: Is there a route for respondents who have no knowledge of or opinion about the object?
keying: Does the set include items keyed in both directions, without negations?
cover_the_construct: Does each item tap a distinct stated domain, with no item a rewording of another?
can_they_know: Is the item asking for something the respondent is likely to have stored and can retrieve?
reference_period: Is there one stated reference period with unambiguous boundaries, short enough for the behaviour?
decompose_with_care: If the item is decomposed, are the sub-categories distinct, non-overlapping and memorable?
how_many_or_how_often: Does the wording match how respondents will arrive at the answer, counting or a rate?
open_number: Is a count or amount collected as an open number with a stated unit, or else with categories free of vague quantifiers?
does_it_apply: Can a respondent who did not do the behaviour, or to whom it does not apply, answer truthfully?
why_sensitive: Is the kind of sensitivity and the expected direction of misreporting stated?
mode_and_privacy: Do the notes address who can hear or see the answer in the stated mode?
forgiving_intro: If a forgiving introduction is used, does it point only toward the under-reported answer and contain no invented fact?
assume_behavior: If the item assumes the behaviour, is "none" or "never" an explicit, easy answer?
ever_then_current: Does the order of ever and current questions match the direction of desirability?
open_or_high_range: Does the response format avoid making a truthful high answer look deviant?
respondent_safety: Is any item whose honest answer could endanger the respondent flagged for local and ethical review?
any_mode: Does the item work as written in the stated mode?
web: Is everything the respondent needs to answer on screen with the question?

Follow every rule you were given. Reply in the format given at the end of this message.

REPLY FORMAT
Return one JSON object. Write findings in English, and write a rewrite in the language of the question. Be brief: nothing outside the fields below is shown to the analyst.

For questions, the object is {"items": [...]}, one entry per question, in the order given. Each entry has:

- "id": the question's own label, or its position.
- "flags": every problem you stand behind, most damaging first; an empty list if there is none. Each flag has:
  - "check": the id of the CHECKLIST check it fails.
  - "stage": "comprehension", "retrieval", "judgment" or "reporting".
  - "level": "fix" if you would revise the question before fielding; "consider" if the problem is real but smaller, or needs the analyst's knowledge.
  - "quote": words copied exactly from the question or its options.
  - "why": at most 25 words: what the respondent cannot do, in plain words.
- "rewrite": one rewrite of the whole question and its options that fixes its fix-level flags and changes nothing else; an empty string when it has no fix-level flag.

For the questionnaire as a whole, the object is {"instrument": [...]}: at most 3 flags of the same shape, each with "questions" (a list of the ids of the questions it concerns) in place of "quote".

Nothing else: no severity, no probe, no test plan, no rewrite of a single flag.

flags.why: Someone who part-owns and part-rents, or has another arrangement, has no clear option, and 'Other' gives no space to say what.
Respondents may count lodgers, students living away or part-time residents differently. This changes the count used for energy use per person.
'Heating' could mean the warmth, the running cost, the controls or the equipment, so respondents may rate different things.
Start and end of 'last winter' are not stated. Depending on when they answer, respondents may think of the current or the previous winter.
Vague frequency words mean different amounts to different people, so answers are not comparable.
People who moved into this home after last winter cannot answer about this home.

items.rewrite: Think about December to February of the most recent winter. In those months, how often was your home too cold for you to be comfortable? Never / Rarely / Sometimes / Often / Always

flags.why: Many people do not know this term, so they may skip it or pick it wrongly. It is not explained on screen.
Two different fuels share one option, so a household using only one of them cannot be told apart in the data.

items.rewrite: What is the main fuel you use to heat your home? If you use more than one, choose the one you use most. Mains gas / Electricity / Heating oil / Liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) / Wood or coal / Heat network (heat piped in from a shared central boiler) / Other / Don't know

flags.quote: Has your household cut back on heating to save money?
flags.why: No time period is given, so respondents may think of any time from last week to years ago.

items.rewrite: In the last 12 months, has your household cut back on heating to save money? Please include times when you kept the heating off on purpose. Yes / No

flags.why: Many households pay quarterly, by fixed direct debit or by top-up, so they may not know last month's spend. No 'don't know' route is offered.
Two separate bills must be added together in the respondent's head, which invites errors and guessing.
Homes with no mains gas, or with bills included in rent, have no true answer for one or both.
Not everyone knows this billing term, so some will leave the charge out.

items.rewrite: About how much did your household spend last month on each of these? Look at a recent bill or your account if you can. Include standing charges (the fixed daily charge on your bill). Enter each amount in pounds. Electricity: £____ (or tick: None / Don't know). Mains gas: £____ (or tick: None / Don't know).

flags.quote: Definitely / Probably / Probably not / Definitely not
flags.why: People who do not know what help exists must still choose a side. There is no 'don't know' option.

flags.quote: Definitely / Probably / Probably not / Definitely not
flags.why: 'Definitely' does not say what it refers to. Respondents must work out that it means yes, enough.

flags.quote: the government is doing enough to help households
flags.why: 'The government' and 'help' are not specified, so respondents may think of different bodies or measures.

items.rewrite: Do you think the government is doing enough to help households with their energy bills, or not? Yes, definitely / Yes, probably / No, probably not / No, definitely not / Don't know

flags.quote: Obviously, high energy bills are caused by greedy energy companies.
flags.why: 'Obviously' and 'greedy' push respondents toward agreeing. The statement presents blame as established fact.

flags.quote: How much do you agree or disagree with this statement?
flags.why: Agree-disagree invites agreeing whatever the content. A question about how much blame energy companies deserve would measure the view directly.

flags.quote: high energy bills are caused by
flags.why: Assumes the respondent regards bills as high and that one cause explains them.
Respondents with no view on causes have no 'don't know' option, only a midpoint that also means a balanced view.

items.rewrite: How much, if at all, do you think energy companies are to blame for the level of household energy bills? A great deal / Quite a lot / Only a little / Not at all / Don't know

flags.quote: and did these changes lower your bills?
flags.why: Asks what was done and what effect it had. A respondent who made changes but saw no fall cannot answer with one Yes or No.

flags.quote: Have you made any changes to your home to save energy
flags.why: No time period is given. Respondents may count any change ever made, including by earlier occupants or a landlord.

flags.quote: did these changes lower your bills
flags.why: Bills also change with prices and weather, so respondents can only guess what effect the changes had.

items.rewrite: In the last 5 years, have you made any changes to your home to save energy, such as loft insulation, double glazing or a smart thermostat? Yes / No

flags.quote: Please answer even if you rent.
flags.why: Renters, flat dwellers and people who already have panels may be unable to install. The instruction pushes them to give an invented answer.

flags.quote: Very likely / Fairly likely / Fairly unlikely / Very unlikely
flags.why: No true answer for people who already have panels or cannot install them. No 'don't know' option.

items.rewrite: How likely are you to install solar panels on your home in the next five years? Very likely / Fairly likely / Fairly unlikely / Very unlikely / I already have solar panels / I cannot install them (for example, I rent or live in a flat) / Don't know

flags.why: Assumes everyone has a paid job and one workplace away from home. Retired, unemployed and home-based people have no true answer.
'Normal' is not defined, so people with changing hours or hybrid working may answer for different weeks.

items.rewrite: In a normal week, on how many days do you travel to a place of work outside your home? 0 / 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 / 6 / 7 / I am not in paid work

flags.why: People who do not travel to work, or are not in work, have no true option. Routing from the previous question is not stated.
It is unclear whether 'longest' means distance or time, so people using several modes may choose differently.

items.rewrite: How do you usually travel to your place of work? Choose the way you use for the longest part of the journey. Car or van / Bus or coach / Train or tram / Bicycle / Walk / Motorcycle / Other / I do not travel to a place of work

one_thing: Does the question ask about exactly one thing, so that no respondent would want to answer its parts differently?
